title: Whole Numbers up to One Million: Place Value, Figures and Words
seo_title: Whole Numbers up to 1,000,000 – Primary 4 Mathematics Worksheets with Answers (NERDC)
standard_text: Count, read and write whole numbers up to one million in figures and in words; identify the place value of digits up to one million. (summary of the NERDC Primary 4 Mathematics curriculum)
meta_desc: Free Primary 4 maths worksheets on whole numbers up to one million: place value, value of a digit, numbers in figures and in words, expanded form and counting in thousands. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Read big numbers in groups of three digits.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Each digit has a place (units, tens, hundreds, thousands, ten thousands, hundred thousands) and a value.
  • In 482,375 the 8 is in the ten thousands place, so its value is 80,000.
  • Read big numbers in groups of three: 482 thousand, 375 → four hundred and eighty-two thousand, three hundred and seventy-five.

Examples

Example

Value of 6 in 361,042

6 is in the ten thousands place

Answer: 60,000

Example

Write 205,040 in words

205 thousand and 40

Answer: two hundred and five thousand, forty

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Giving the digit, not its valueThe value of 6 in 361,042 is 60,000, not 6.
Leaving out a zeroTwo hundred and five thousand is 205,000.
Forgetting the commasPut a comma after every three digits from the right.

faq.q: Why do we put commas in big numbers?
faq.a: They split the digits into groups of three so the number is easy to read.

faq.q: What does a zero do in a number?
faq.a: It holds a place so the other digits keep their values.

items.q: What is the value of the digit 9 in this number?
items.e: The 9 is in the hundreds place, so its value is 9 × 100 = 900. The digit is 9, but its value is 900.
